feed.title: Andre Romero-Carey — Notes
feed.subtitle: Technical notes on verifying AI-assisted software without reading code, multi-agent coordination with CI oracles, input validation, and machine-checked Lean 4 verification.

entry.title: Coordinating Coding Agents and Catching Real Bugs with CI Oracles
entry.summary: How a non-coder isolates parallel coding agents with wcp and uses multi-version Linux GitHub Actions CI as an independent oracle to catch five real cross-platform, concurrency, and floating-point bugs across wcp (232 tests) and luck-filter (55 tests).

entry.title: Verifying AI-Assisted Contributions Without Reading Code
entry.summary: How a non-coder verifies AI-assisted open-source work with independent oracles across three verified case studies: modelcontextprotocol/inspector#2980 (merged in PR #3016), google-deepmind/formal-conjectures#7590 (backed by open-proofs), and the four-invoice behavioral walkthrough in inbox-guard v0.1.0.

entry.title: Checking Untrusted AI-Authored Lean 4 Proofs
entry.summary: Why lake build plus a sorry grep fails when unattended coding agents write Lean 4 proofs. Walks through the 5-layer proof checker in open-proofs, its 48 self-test checks (41 negative tamper/bypass checks plus 7 positive controls), scope limits, and the negation proofs behind google-deepmind/formal-conjectures#7590.

entry.title: Screening Untrusted Office Inputs Before LLM Triage
entry.summary: Design, code mechanics, and known limitations of inbox-guard: magic-byte attachment checks, Unicode U+202E and Windows/SMB filename spoofing, accounting-safe OWASP CSV neutralization, WHATWG HTML5 comment and linear CSS hidden-content scanning, Plane-14 Unicode Tag stripping, and randomized session-scoped PII tokenization.
